facts.statement: The species Kuntur cardenasi was described by Stucchi and colleagues in 2015.
facts.quote:
genus: Kuntur
species: cardenasi
authority: Stucchi et al., 2015

facts.statement: Kuntur belongs to the family Cathartidae.
Kuntur was an extinct bird of the family Cathartidae that lived in South America during the Tortonian stage of the Miocene epoch.
facts.quote: Kuntur is an extinct monotypic genus of cathartid bird that lived in South America during the Tortonian stage of the Miocene epoch.

facts.statement: Kuntur lived between 11.63 and 7.246 million years ago during the Tortonian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Tortonian to Tortonian (11.63 to 7.246 million years ago)

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Kuntur has been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.

rejected.statement: The specific name cardenasi honors Santiago de Cárdenas, the first Peruvian naturalist to study condors.
rejected.quote: The specific epithet refers to Santiago de Cárdenas, the first Peruvian naturalist to study condors.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Cárdenas the first Peruvian naturalist to study condors'
